question: What exactly are intrinsic sugars?

options.A: Sugars naturally bound inside the cell walls of whole foods
options.B: Chemical preservatives used to extend shelf life in drinks
options.C: Refined sweeteners added to foods during factory processing
options.D: Artificial sweeteners that contain zero calories

explanation: You can think of intrinsic sugars as the good guys! They are safely locked inside whole, unprocessed foods like fruits and vegetables, right alongside healthy fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h1)

question: Why do intrinsic sugars digest much slower than free sugars?

options.A: They bind to red blood cells and delay energy release
options.B: They are protected by the natural cellular structure and fiber of the food
options.C: They bypass the stomach and enter the small intestine immediately
options.D: They require no digestive enzymes to break them down into glucose

explanation: Because the fiber and cell walls are intact, your digestive system has to put in extra work. This slows down how fast sugar enters your bloodstream, giving you steady energy! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h1)

question: Which organ gets overwhelmed and converts surplus dietary sugars into fat?
explanation: Your liver handles the heavy lifting when processing dietary sugars. When it gets overloaded, it converts those extra sugars directly into fat molecules. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h2)

question: How does eating too much sugar over a long time lead to insulin resistance?

options.A: Sugar molecules coat the pancreas and permanently stop it from making any digestive enzymes
options.B: Constant high blood sugar forces the pancreas to oversecrete insulin until body cells stop responding
options.C: High sugar levels destroy every insulin receptor in the liver instantly
options.D: The kidneys block all insulin from entering the bloodstream to protect the heart

explanation: Imagine constantly shouting at someone—eventually, they stop listening! High glucose levels force your pancreas to pump out so much insulin that your body cells eventually tune it out. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h2)

question: What is the WHO's strong recommendation for daily free sugar intake?
explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) advises keeping free sugars below 10% of your total daily energy intake to help prevent health issues like obesity and tooth decay. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h3)

question: For an adult needing 2,000 calories a day, roughly how many grams of free sugar is the stricter 5% WHO target?
explanation: Ten percent of 2,000 calories is 200 calories (or 50 grams of sugar). The conditional 5% target cuts that amount right in half to just 25 grams! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h3)

question: When reading ingredient labels, which suffix usually tells you an ingredient is a sugar?
explanation: Spotting a sneaky sugar is easier when you know the language! Most simple sugars end in '-ose', like sucrose, lactose, and glucose. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h4)

question: Why do food manufacturers sometimes use multiple different names for sugar on a single ingredient list?

options.A: To divide the total amount so individual sugars appear further down the weight-based ingredient list
options.B: To make the product taste better by combining artificial and natural sweeteners together
options.C: To prevent the food from spoiling too quickly on supermarket shelves
options.D: To comply with strict international laws requiring chemical names for every single food item

explanation: It's a clever marketing trick! By splitting sugar into three or four different names, manufacturers can scatter them down the list so the product looks healthier than it really is. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h4)

question: What is the most effective first step a nurse can suggest to help a patient cut down on hidden sugars?

options.A: Eating only raw vegetables for breakfast and lunch
options.B: Replacing sugary sodas and packaged fruit juices with plain water
options.C: Eliminating all complex carbohydrates from every meal
options.D: Switching from white table sugar to organic raw honey

explanation: Sugary drinks are the biggest source of hidden calories in most diets. Swapping them for water is the easiest and most powerful change a patient can make! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h5)

question: A patient wants to bake a healthier cake with less refined sugar. What is a great nursing suggestion?

options.A: Use mashed ripe bananas or unsweetened applesauce to add natural sweetness and moisture
options.B: Add artificial chemical cleaners to make the dough rise faster
options.C: Double the amount of salt to block the bitter taste of unsweetened flour
options.D: Replace sugar with extra drops of liquid vegetable oil

explanation: Mashed fruits are fantastic baking substitutes! They bring natural sweetness and moisture thanks to their intrinsic sugars and fiber, keeping the cake delicious without refined sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h5)
